About Shomaji & Associates

Shomaji & Associates

Legal Practitioners and Consultants
Trial Advocacy & Litigation Excellence Since 1986

Full-Service Law Practice Based in Dhaka

Shomaji & Associates is a full-service law firm based in Dhaka, Bangladesh. Since 1986, experience in criminal litigation, civil disputes, company disputes, and corporate matters. It is a leading law firm specialized in trial advocacy under the leadership of Ehsanul Haque Shomaji. The Firmâ€™s principal areas of practice encompass international crimes, corruption, money laundering and financial crime, homicide and other serious criminal offences, cybercrime, corporate and commercial criminal litigation, narcotics-related offences, offences involving arms and explosives, including offences under the general and special laws, family matters, and civil matters. The Firm has been engaged in complex and high-profile criminal proceedings, including matters of substantial legal and jurisprudential significance. Its practice is distinguished by a commitment to rigorous legal research, principled advocacy, strategic case preparation, and the effective representation of clients before the competent courts and tribunals throughout Bangladesh.

Ehsanul Haque Shomaji Head of Chambers | Supreme Court of Bangladesh
Chamber Practice Focus

Our Practice Areas

Delivering high-caliber legal counsel and courtroom representation across diverse legal areas in Bangladesh.

Criminal Law

Supreme Court Chamber & High Court Litigation Division

Premier criminal litigation chamber providing specialized trial advocacy, pre-trial advisory, statutory defense, and appellate representation before trial courts, Special Judge Courts, Druto Bichar Tribunals, and the Supreme Court of Bangladesh since 1986.

Detailed Practice Information

Civil Litigation

Original, Revisional, Appellate & Review Jurisdiction

Shomaji & Associates provides strategic trial and appellate representation in complex land and property disputes, title and possession, partition, contractual specific performance, money suits, eviction, and civil appeals under the laws of Bangladesh.

Detailed Practice Information

Corporate Law

Corporate Governance, Financial Crimes, Banking Recovery & Commercial Arbitration

Comprehensive legal representation in financial crimes, Negotiable Instruments (NI Act Sec 138), Artha Rin Adalat, corporate governance, commercial arbitration, M&A restructuring, and banking credit disputes.

Detailed Practice Information

Family Matter

Matrimonial Disputes, Child Custody & Shariah Advisory

Compassionate and rigorous advocacy in marriage, divorce, dower (denmohor), maintenance, child custody, guardianship, dowry defense, and Muslim family law.

Detailed Practice Information

Terms & Conditions

Legal notice and usage terms of Shomaji & Associates

1. General Disclaimer

The materials and information contained on this website are provided for informational and educational purposes only, in accordance with the regulations of the Bangladesh Bar Council. They do not constitute formal legal advice or the establishment of a lawyer-client relationship until a formal vakalatnama or engagement agreement is executed.

2. Confidentiality

Shomaji & Associates treats all initial inquiries and consultation requests with the highest standards of professional secrecy and advocate-client privilege recognized under the Evidence Act 1872.

3. Intellectual Property

All articles, case analyses, branding logos, and content published on this website are the intellectual property of Shomaji & Associates and may not be reproduced without explicit written consent.

Privacy Policy

How Shomaji & Associates protects client data and confidentiality

1. Information Collection

When you submit a consultation request or contact message, we collect your name, phone number, email, and brief case details solely for the purpose of communicating with you and assessing your legal matter.

2. Non-Disclosure & Security

Shomaji & Associates does not sell, rent, or disclose personal client data to third parties. All consultation requests are stored securely on our dedicated servers and handled strictly by our authorized advocates and staff.

3. Contact & Rights

You may request the deletion or update of your inquiry records at any time by contacting us directly at info@shomaji.com.

Chamber Openings

Opportunities at Shomaji & Associates

We invite passionate legal minds who seek to master courtroom advocacy, criminal litigation, civil disputes, and corporate practice.

Law Graduates Week-Long

1. Internships

Eligibility & Structure

Fresh law graduates seeking intensive hands-on chamber experience and courtroom orientation.

How to Apply:

Fresh law graduates may apply for a week-long internship at Shomaji & Associates by making an application to the Head of Chambers. The application should be accompanied by a current CV of the applicant.

  • Direct exposure to trial preparation & legal drafting
  • Supreme Court & Sessions Court observation
  • Official Certificate upon successful completion
Apply via Email (info@shomaji.com)
Learned Advocates Full-Time Chamber Associate

2. Associate

Eligibility & Engagement

Qualified learned advocates seeking to participate in high-stakes litigation, trial advocacy, and Supreme Court practice.

How to Apply:

Qualified learned advocates may apply to become associates at Shomaji & Associates by making an application to the Head of Chambers. The application should be accompanied by a current CV of the applicant. Interested candidates are requested to contact the chamber for an appointment.

  • Mentorship under Ehsanul Haque Shomaji
  • Complex criminal litigation, ACC defense & ICT-BD
  • High Court appellate practice & legal research
Apply via Email (info@shomaji.com)
Direct Submission

Application Submission & Appointments

All applications must be addressed to the Head of Chambers, Ehsanul Haque Shomaji, accompanied by an up-to-date Curriculum Vitae (CV) outlining academic credentials, bar enrollment details (where applicable), and relevant experience.

01
International Crimes

International Crimes Practice (ICT-BD)

Shomaji & Associates provides legal representation, legal consultation and specialised legal research in matters arising under international criminal law, including proceedings before the International Crimes Tribunal of Bangladesh and the relevant appellate forums, subject to the scope of engagement and applicable law. The practice encompasses complex legal issues concerning crimes against humanity, genocide, war crimes and other offences falling within the jurisdiction of the competent tribunal.

Statutory & Legal Framework

Governing Acts, Ordinances & Statutory Rules

The practice is grounded in the International Crimes (Tribunals) Act, 1973, the International Crimes Tribunal Rules of Procedure, and other applicable laws of Bangladesh. Depending on the issues arising in a particular matter, relevant international legal sources may include the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court, 1998, the Geneva Conventions of 1949 and their applicable Additional Protocols, customary international law, international humanitarian law, and the jurisprudence of domestic and international courts and tribunals. The relevance and legal effect of each source are assessed in accordance with the applicable law, the jurisdiction of the forum and the circumstances of the proceedings.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach

Courtroom Representation & Evidentiary Procedure

The firmâ€™s services include legal representation before the competent forums, professional legal consultation, conduct of trial proceedings and advanced legal research on substantive, procedural and evidentiary questions arising in international criminal proceedings. Research and case preparation may involve analysing indictments, charge-framing orders, investigation materials, witness statements, documentary evidence, judicial precedents and relevant international legal authorities. Depending on the engagement, the firm may also undertake the preparation of legal opinions, case analyses, written submissions and research memoranda, together with legal work relating to trial proceedings, appellate challenges and other remedies available under the applicable law. All work is undertaken with a focus on rigorous legal analysis, accurate interpretation of the governing legal framework, careful assessment of the evidentiary record and observance of the applicable procedural safeguards.

02
Financial Crimes & ACC

Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) Related Practice

Shomaji & Associates provides legal representation in proceedings involving allegations of corruption, illicit enrichment, abuse of public office, embezzlement and financial misconduct under the laws of Bangladesh. The practice encompasses criminal litigation before the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) and Special Judge Courts.

Statutory & Legal Framework

Governing Acts, Ordinances & Statutory Rules

The practice is governed principally by the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004, the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958, the Money Laundering Prevention Act, 2012, the Penal Code, 1860, and other applicable legislation governing corruption-related offences, investigation, prosecution and trial.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach

Courtroom Representation & Evidentiary Procedure

Our litigation approach is grounded in a rigorous assessment of the statutory ingredients of each alleged offence, the prosecutionâ€™s evidentiary foundation, and the legal basis for attributing criminal liability to each accused. We examine the complaint, FIR, investigation reports, charge sheet, witness statements, documentary evidence, financial records and relevant expert materials to identify evidentiary gaps, inconsistencies, questions of admissibility and deficiencies in the proof of essential elements. Particular attention is given to allegations involving acquisition of assets disproportionate to known sources of income, illicit enrichment, abuse of public office, misappropriation of funds, financial transactions and alleged conspiracy or complicity. Depending on the facts and applicable law, our analysis may address the source and ownership of assets, the distinction between suspicion and legally sufficient proof, the individual role and state of mind of each accused, and whether the evidence establishes the necessary connection between the accused and the alleged offence.

Murder and Serious Offences

Statutory & Legal Framework

The practice is governed principally by the Penal Code, 1860, the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, the Evidence Act, 1872, and applicable special legislation. It includes proceedings under relevant provisions concerning homicide, offences against the person, robbery, dacoity, criminal breach of trust and other serious crimes.

Litigation Strategy & Chamber Approach

Courtroom Representation & Evidentiary Procedure

The firm undertakes fact-specific legal analysis of the alleged offence, the prosecution's evidentiary case, individual criminal responsibility, applicable statutory defences and legally sustainable grounds for challenge or appeal. Its approach emphasises rigorous legal research, careful examination of the evidentiary record and professional courtroom advocacy, with due regard to the presumption of innocence, procedural safeguards and the right to a fair trial under the laws of Bangladesh.

Executive Biography & Chamber Leadership

Head of Chambers, Shomaji & Associates | Leading 23 Trial Advocates & Litigators

Advocate Ehsanul Haque Shomaji has devoted his professional career to criminal law practice, prosecution leadership, anti-corruption enforcement, and high-level legal consultancy. He is the founder and Head of Chambers of Shomaji & Associates, one of the premier law chambers in Dhaka, Bangladesh, where 23 advocates work under his leadership.

Through his long-standing service in Bangladeshâ€™s justice sector, Mr. Shomaji has acquired specialized knowledge and skills in criminal litigation, prosecution strategy, evidence law, corporate compliance advisory, and institutional legal reform.

Biography & Chamber Experience

Dr. Borhan Uddin Khan is currently a Professor in the Department of Law, University of Dhaka and was a former Dean of the Faculty of Law (2006-2010) and Chairman of the Department of Law (2015-2017). He is also an Advisor and Adjunct Professor, in the Department of Law, Independent University, Bangladesh (IUB) with responsibility to lead and head the Department. Borhan holds an LL.M. in Public International Law (1990) from the London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE), University of London and Ph.D. (1995) from the School of Oriental and African Studies (SOAS), University of London. In order to pursue higher studies and research, he has availed: Commonwealth Scholarship, British Council Fellowship, UN/UNITAR Fellowship in Public International Law, UNHCR Sponsorship, ICRC Sponsorship, ILO Sponsorship and Scholarship from The Hague Academy of International Law.

Borhan enrolled himself as a lawyer with the Bangladesh Bar Council in 1986 and to the High Court Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh in 1988. In 1989, he joined the Department of Law, University of Dhaka as a Lecturer after completing LL.B. (Hons.) and LL.M. from the same University. He is a founder member and former Vice President of the Asian Society of International Law and also the founder and current President of its Bangladesh Chapter. He also holds membership in the American Society of International Law (ASIL) and the International Law Association (ILA).

Borhanâ€™s research interests include: International Human Rights and Humanitarian Law, International Refugee Law, International Criminal Law, International Labor Law and Minority Rights. As a Consultant of the Ministry of Law Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, he codified the laws of Bangladesh (1939-2005), published in 2007 as The Bangladesh Code (36 Volumes). He has co-authored book on, Protection of Minorities: Regimes, Norms and Issues in South Asia, (Cambridge Scholars Publishing, 2012) and co-edited Revisiting the Geneva Conventions: 1949-2019, (Brill/Nijhoff, 2020). His co-edited book on Human Rights and International Criminal Law is forthcoming in 2021.

Professor Borhan Uddin Khan received in 2017 â€˜The LSE Outstanding Alumni Volunteer Awardâ€™ from his alma mater, the London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE), University of London.

Practice Specialties

International Human Rights & Humanitarian Law, Public International Law & International Criminal Law, International Refugee Law & Labor Law, Minority Rights & International Law Norms, Codification of Bangladesh Laws (The Bangladesh Code, 36 Volumes), Supreme Court High Court Division Advocacy (Since 1988)

  • LL.M. â€” Department of Law, University of Dhaka

Professional Profile
Barrister Milhanur Rahman is a legal practitioner with over 9 years of experience in corporate and commercial law, criminal and civil litigation, banking and finance disputes, debt recovery, and dispute resolution in Bangladesh. Called to the Bar of England and Wales through the Honourable Society of Lincolnâ€™s Inn in 2017, he combines an international legal education with practical experience in Bangladeshâ€™s legal and regulatory environment.
His practice encompasses corporate advisory, commercial transactions, contractual documentation, criminal defence, civil litigation, financial disputes, and constitutional remedies. He advises clients on complex legal issues, develops case-specific litigation strategies, and prepares legal submissions and commercial instruments with an emphasis on accuracy, procedural compliance, and practical outcomes.
With experience in both contentious and non-contentious legal work, Barrister Milhanur provides legal services to individuals, businesses, and corporate clients, addressing their requirements through litigation, negotiation, advisory services, and alternative dispute resolution.
Areas of Practice
1. Criminal Litigation
Barrister Milhanurâ€™s criminal litigation practice focuses on defence strategy, trial preparation, procedural remedies, evidentiary analysis, and the protection of the legal rights of accused persons. His approach involves a detailed assessment of the allegations, the evidence relied upon by the prosecution, the legality of investigative and judicial proceedings, and the availability of remedies under the applicable law.
His areas of criminal practice and related legal work include:
- Criminal Defence and Trial Advocacy: Preparation of defence cases, analysis of prosecution evidence, cross-examination strategy, witness credibility, and legal submissions before competent criminal courts.
- Bail and Criminal Procedure: Regular bail, anticipatory or pre-arrest bail where legally available, remand-related proceedings, discharge applications, and other remedies under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898.
- Serious Criminal Offences: Defence-related legal work involving allegations of murder, assault, criminal intimidation, cheating, criminal breach of trust, forgery, and other offences under the Penal Code, 1860 and applicable special legislation.
- Criminal Complaints and Magistracy Proceedings: Complaint cases, proceedings arising from police reports, cognizance, discharge, and other procedural issues before the Magistracy.
- Appeals, Revisions and High Court Proceedings: Criminal appeals, revisions, and applications before the High Court Division or other competent courts, subject to jurisdiction and applicable procedural requirements.
- Women and Children Repression Prevention Cases: Legal work relating to proceedings under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act, 2000.
- Anti-Corruption Proceedings: Legal research, defence preparation, and representation, where authorised, in matters involving the Anti-Corruption Commission and applicable anti-corruption legislation.
- Evidence and Forensic Issues: Examination of documentary evidence, disputed signatures, forensic reports, inconsistencies in witness statements, and material defects in investigation or trial.
- Constitutional Remedies in Criminal Matters: Legal work concerning unlawful detention, abuse of process, jurisdictional errors, and alleged violations of fundamental rights, where an appropriate remedy is maintainable.
His criminal litigation approach emphasises careful scrutiny of the prosecution case, identification of material legal and procedural defects, application of relevant statutory provisions and judicial precedents, and the protection of fair-trial rights.
2. Corporate and Commercial Law
Barrister Milhanur advises on corporate legal matters, commercial transactions, contractual obligations, regulatory compliance, and business-related disputes. His work includes legal risk assessment, contract negotiation, transactional support, corporate restructuring, and the preparation of legal documentation tailored to commercial objectives.
His corporate practice includes:

Judicial Decision Analysis

Judicial Decision Analysis: Procedural Standards in Money Laundering Adjudication

By Ehsanul Haque Shomaji January 05, 2025 1,843 Views
An expert analysis of evidentiary standards, judicial precedents, and international compliance frameworks under the Money Laundering Prevention Act.

The adjudication of financial crimes and money laundering allegations in Bangladesh demands an exacting standard of evidentiary scrutiny. With the evolving statutory architecture under the Money Laundering Prevention Act, courts and practitioners must balance stringent regulatory measures with the fundamental procedural safeguards guaranteed to every accused person.

Core Evidentiary Principles

Establishing the predicate offence and tracing illicit proceeds requires rigorous financial documentation rather than circumstantial presumption. The burden of proof resting upon the prosecution remains paramount, and statutory presumptions must be applied in strict alignment with constitutional protections.

Legislative Analysis

Legislative Analysis: Modernising the Criminal Justice System through CrPC Reforms

By Ehsanul Haque Shomaji January 12, 2025 2,453 Views
Insights into structural amendments to the Code of Criminal Procedure aimed at expediting trials, modernising bail provisions, and strengthening judicial efficiency.

The Code of Criminal Procedure forms the bedrock of the administration of criminal justice in Bangladesh. Modernising this century-old statutory framework is essential to addressing case backlogs, delays in pre-trial investigations, and procedural bottlenecks that impact both victims and the accused.

Key Areas of Proposed Reform

Codifying clearer standards for pre-trial bail, incorporating electronic evidence protocols, and establishing structured timelines for investigation reports are crucial milestones toward a fair and transparent judicial process.

Biography & Chamber Experience

Shaikh Nazmul Alam is a former Senior District & Sessions Judge of Jessore (Jashore), Bangladesh. Having served in Bangladesh's judicial service with distinguished honor, he presided over numerous landmark trials, evidentiary deliberations, and complex civil and criminal proceedings.

Throughout his esteemed judicial career, Judge Alam has been widely respected for his adherence to the rule of law, meticulous evaluation of judicial evidence, and deep jurisprudential knowledge. Following his retirement from active judicial service, he serves as a Senior Judicial Advisor to Shomaji & Associates, providing authoritative strategic insight on trial preparation, judicial procedure, and high-stakes dispute resolution.

Ehsanul Haque Shomaji appointed special prosecutorial adviser to Home Ministry

By Dhaka Tribune December 19, 2024 3,891 Views
Senior criminal law practitioner Ehsanul Haque Shomaji has been appointed as a special prosecutorial adviser to the Ministry of Home Affairs with the status of Attorney General for Bangladesh.

The Ministry of Home Affairs has appointed senior Supreme Court advocate Ehsanul Haque Shomaji as its Special Prosecutorial Adviser with status equivalent to the Attorney General for Bangladesh.

In this high-level role, Mr. Shomaji advises on complex criminal prosecutions, reviews police investigation files, and coordinates national prosecutorial integrity across investigating agencies.

Advocate Shomaji turns down Dhaka metropolis public prosecutor role

By Dhaka Tribune August 29, 2024 3,242 Views
Senior lawyer Ehsanul Haque Shomaji has formally declined the position of Public Prosecutor of Dhaka Metropolitan Sessions Court to maintain professional independence and client commitments.

Advocate Ehsanul Haque Shomaji declined the post of Metropolitan Public Prosecutor of Dhaka, explaining that his existing legal commitments to various defense clients would create potential conflicts of interest, adhering strictly to the highest standards of legal ethics.

By The Daily Observer August 28, 2024 2,561 Views
The Ministry of Law has officially appointed eminent criminal defense counsel Advocate Ehsanul Haque Shomaji as the new Metropolitan Public Prosecutor of Dhaka.

The Daily Observer reported on the appointment of Ehsanul Haque Shomaji as Metropolitan PP, citing his long track record of prosecutorial leadership during the 2007-2009 Caretaker Government regime.
